rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: [ F56 SECTION B U.K. CAA REQUIREMENTS

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.005 Scope U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: This section establishes the conditions for conducting the certification, oversight and enforcement tasks as well as the administrative and management system requirements to be followed by the CAA.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.115 Oversight documentation U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must provide all the standards, rules, technical publications, and related documents to the relevant personnel in order to allow them to perform their tasks and to discharge their responsibilities.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.120 Means of compliance U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must develop an acceptable means of compliance that may be used to establish compliance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Alternative means of compliance may be used by an organisation to establish compliance with this Regulation when approved by the CAA.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.135 Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Without prejudice to Regulation (EU) No 376/2014, the CAA must implement a system to appropriately collect, analyse and disseminate safety information.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Upon receiving the information referred to in point (a), the CAA must take adequate measures to address the safety problem.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must immediately notify measures taken under point (b) to all organisations which need to comply with them under Regulation (EU) 2018/1139.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.200 Management system U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must establish and maintain a management system, including as a minimum:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: policies and procedures set out in writing and kept on record to describe its organisation and the means and methods for establishing compliance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1139. The procedures must be kept up to date, and serve as the basic working documents within the CAA for all its related tasks;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: a sufficient number of personnel to perform its tasks and discharge its responsibilities. A system must be in place to plan the availability of personnel in order to ensure the proper completion of all tasks;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: personnel that are qualified to perform their allocated tasks and that have the necessary knowledge and experience and receive initial and recurrent training to ensure continuing competency;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: adequate facilities and office accommodation for personnel to perform their allocated tasks;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: a function to monitor the compliance of the management system with the relevant requirements, and the adequacy of the procedures, including the establishment of an internal audit process and a safety risk management process. Compliance monitoring must include a system for feedback of audit findings to the senior management of the CAA to ensure the implementation of corrective actions as necessary;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: a person or group of persons having a responsibility to the senior management of the CAA for the compliance monitoring function.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must, for each field of activity, including the management system, appoint one or more persons with the overall responsibility for the management of the relevant tasks.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.205 Allocation of tasks to qualified entities U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA may allocate tasks, related to the initial certification or to the continuing oversight of organisations subject to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to qualified entities. When allocating tasks, the CAA must ensure that it has:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: put a system in place to initially and continuously assess whether the qualified entity complies with Annex VI to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: established a written agreement with the qualified entity, approved by both parties at the appropriate management level, which stipulates:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the tasks to be performed;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (ii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the declarations, reports and records to be provided;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the technical conditions to be met when performing such tasks;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iv)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the related liability coverage;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the protection given to the information acquired when carrying out such tasks.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must ensure that the internal audit process and safety risk management process established pursuant to point 145.B.200(a)(5) cover all the certification and continuing oversight tasks performed by the qualified entity on its behalf.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.210 Changes in the management system U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must have a system in place to identify the changes that affect its capability to perform its tasks and discharge its responsibilities as defined in Regulation (EU) 2018/1139. That system must enable the CAA to take action necessary to ensure that its management system remains adequate and effective.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must update its management system in a timely manner to reflect any changes to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to ensure its effective implementation.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.220 Record keeping U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must establish a record-keeping system that allows the adequate storage, accessibility and reliable traceability of:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the management system’s documented policies and procedures;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the training, qualifications and authorisations of its personnel;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the allocation of tasks, covering the elements required by point 145.B.205, as well as the details of tasks allocated;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: certification processes and continuing oversight of certified organisations, including:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the application for an organisation certificate;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (ii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the CAA’s continuing oversight programme, including all the assessments, audits and inspection records;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the organisation certificate, including any changes to it;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iv)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: a copy of the oversight programme, listing the dates when audits are due and when audits were carried out;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: copies of all formal correspondence;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (vi)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: recommendations for the issue or continuation of a certificate, details of findings and actions taken by the organisations to close those findings, including the date of closure, enforcement actions and observations;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (vii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: any assessment, audit and inspection report issued by a competent authority of a third country;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (viii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: copies of all the organisation MOEs or manuals, and of any amendments to them;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (ix)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: copies of any other documents approved by the CAA;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: documents supporting the use of alternative means of compliance;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: safety information provided in accordance with point 145.B.125 and follow-up measures;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the use of safeguard and flexibility provisions in accordance with Articles 70, 71(1) and 76(4) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must maintain a list of all the organisation certificates it has issued.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: All the records referred to in points (a) and (b) must be kept for a minimum period of 5 years, subject to data protection law.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.300 Oversight principles U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must verify:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: compliance with the requirements that are applicable to organisations, prior to issuing an organisation certificate;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: continued compliance with the applicable requirements of the organisations it has certified;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the implementation of appropriate safety measures mandated by the CAA in accordance with point 145.B.135(c).

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: This verification must:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: be supported by documentation specifically intended to provide personnel responsible for oversight with guidance to perform their functions;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: provide the organisations concerned with the results of oversight activities;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: be based on assessments, audits and inspections and, if needed, unannounced inspections;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: provide the CAA with the evidence needed in case further action is required, including the measures provided for in point 145.B.350.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must establish the scope of the oversight set out in points (a) and (b) taking into account the results of past oversight activities and the safety priorities.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must collect and process any information deemed necessary for performing oversight activities.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.305 Oversight programme U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must establish and maintain an oversight programme covering the oversight activities required by point 145.B.300.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The oversight programme must take into account the specific nature of the organisation, the complexity of its activities, and the results of past certification and oversight activities, and it must be based on the assessment of the associated risks. It must include, within each oversight planning cycle:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: assessments, audits and inspections, including, as appropriate:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: management system assessments and process audits;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (ii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: product audits of a relevant sample of the maintenance carried out by the organisation;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: sampling of the airworthiness reviews performed;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (iv)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: unannounced inspections;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: meetings convened between the accountable manager and the CAA to ensure that both parties remain informed of all significant issues.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The oversight planning cycle must not exceed 24 months.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Notwithstanding point (c), the oversight planning cycle may be extended to 36 months if the CAA has established that during the previous 24 months:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the organisation has demonstrated that it can effectively identify aviation safety hazards and manage the associated risks;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: the organisation has continuously demonstrated compliance with point 145.A.85 and it has full control over all changes;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: no level 1 findings have been issued;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: all corrective actions have been implemented within the time period that was accepted or extended by the CAA as provided for in point 145.B.350.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Notwithstanding points (c) and (d), the oversight planning cycle may be further extended to a maximum of 48 months if, in addition to the conditions provided in points (d)(1) to (4), the organisation has established, and the CAA has approved, an effective continuous system for reporting to the CAA on the safety performance and regulatory compliance of the organisation itself.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The oversight planning cycle may be shortened if there is evidence that the safety performance of the organisation has decreased.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The oversight programme must include records of the dates when assessments, audits, inspections and meetings are due, and when assessments, audits, inspections and meetings have been effectively carried out.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: At the completion of each oversight planning cycle, the CAA must issue a recommendation report on the continuation of the approval, reflecting the results of the oversight.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.310 Initial certification procedure U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Upon receiving an application from an organisation for the initial issue of a certificate, the CAA must verify the organisation’s compliance with the applicable requirements.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must convene a meeting with the accountable manager of the applicant at least once during the investigation for initial certification to ensure that that person understands their role and accountability.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must record all the findings issued, closure actions as well as the recommendations for the issue of the certificate.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must confirm to the organisation in writing all the findings raised during the verification. For initial certification, all findings must be corrected to the satisfaction of the CAA before the certificate can be issued.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: When satisfied that the organisation complies with the applicable requirements, the CAA may:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: issue the certificate in Appendix III (CAA Form 3-145) in accordance with the class and rating system provided for in Appendix II;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: formally approve the MOE.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The certificate reference number must be included on the CAA Form 3-145 certificate.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The certificate must be issued for an unlimited duration. The privileges and the scope of the activities that the organisation is approved to conduct, including any limitations as applicable, must be specified in the terms of approval attached to the certificate.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: To enable the organisation to implement changes without prior CAA approval in accordance with point [ F57 145.A.85(c) ] , the CAA must approve the relevant MOE procedure that sets out the scope of such changes and describes how such changes will be managed and notified to the CAA.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Textual Amendments

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: F57 Word in Annex 2 point 145.B.310(h) substituted (1.12.2025) by The Aviation Safety (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (S.I. 2025/1150) , regs. 1(2) , 2(3)(b)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.330 Changes – organisations U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Upon receiving an application for a change that requires prior approval, the CAA must verify the organisation’s compliance with the applicable requirements before issuing the approval.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must establish the conditions under which the organisation may operate during the change unless the CAA determines that the organisation’s certificate needs to be suspended.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: When it is satisfied that the organisation complies with the applicable requirements, the CAA must approve the change.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Without prejudice to any additional enforcement measures, if the organisation implements changes requiring prior approval without having received the approval of the CAA pursuant to point (c), the CAA must consider the need to suspend, limit or revoke the organisation’s certificate.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: For changes not requiring prior approval, the CAA must include the review of such changes in its continuing oversight in accordance with the principles set out in point 145.B.300. If any non-compliance is found, the CAA may notify the organisation, request further changes, and act in accordance with point 145.B.350.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 145.B.350 Findings and corrective actions; observations U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must have a system in place to analyse findings for their safety significance.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must issue a level 1 finding when any significant non-compliance is detected with the applicable requirements of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, with the organisation’s procedures or manuals, or with the organisation’s certificate including the terms of approval, which lowers safety or seriously endangers flight safety.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Level 1 findings include:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: any failure to grant the CAA access to the organisation’s facilities referred to in point 145.A.140 during normal operating hours and after two written requests;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: obtaining the organisation certificate or maintaining its validity by falsification of the submitted documentary evidence;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: any evidence of malpractice or fraudulent use of the organisation certificate;

rows.text: The CAA must issue a level 2 finding when any non-compliance is detected with the applicable requirements of Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, with the organisation’s procedures or manuals, or with the organisation’s certificate including the terms of approval, which is not classified as a level 1 finding.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Where a finding is detected during oversight or by any other means, the CAA must, without prejudice to any additional action required by Regulation (EU) 2018/1139, communicate the finding in writing to the organisation and request corrective action to address the non-compliance identified.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Where there are any level 1 findings, the CAA must take immediate and appropriate action to prohibit or limit the activities of the organisation involved and, if appropriate, it must take action to revoke the certificate or to limit or suspend it in whole or in part, depending on the extent of the level 1 finding, until successful corrective action has been taken by the organisation.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Where there are any level 2 findings, the CAA must:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: grant the organisation a corrective action implementation period appropriate to the nature of the finding which must not be more than 3 months. The period must commence from the date of the written communication referred to in point (e). The CAA may extend the corrective action implementation period referred to in point (e) provided the relevant organisation has agreed a corrective action plan with the CAA;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: (ii)

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: assess the corrective action plan and implementation plan proposed by the organisation and accept them if they are sufficient to address the non-compliance.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: If the organisation fails to submit an acceptable corrective action plan, or fails to perform the corrective action within the time period accepted or extended by the CAA, the CAA must raise the finding to level 1 and action must be taken as laid down in point (e)(1).

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must record all the findings that it has raised or that have been communicated to it and, where applicable, the enforcement measures it has applied, as well as all corrective actions and the dates of the action closures for all the findings.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA may issue observations for any of the following cases not requiring level 1 or level 2 findings:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: for any item whose performance has been assessed to be ineffective;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: when it has been identified that an item has the potential to cause a non-compliance under point (b) or (d);

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: when suggestions or improvements are of interest for the overall safety performance of the organisation.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The CAA must communicate the observations issued under this point in writing to the organisation and must keep a record of those observations.

rows.text: Except as stated otherwise for the smallest organisations referred to in point (m), the table in point (l) provides the possible classes and ratings to be used to establish the terms of approval of the certificate of the organisation approved in accordance with Annex II (Part-145). An organisation must be granted terms of approval that range from a single class and rating with limitations to all classes and ratings with limitations.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: In addition to the table in point (l), each maintenance organisation is required to indicate its scope of work in its MOE.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Within the approval classes and ratings established by the CAA, the scope of work specified in the MOE defines the exact limits of its approval. It is therefore essential that the approval classes and ratings and the organisation’s scope of work match.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: A “ category A class rating ” means that the maintenance organisation may carry out maintenance on aircraft and components (including engines, auxiliary power units (APUs) or both), in accordance with the aircraft maintenance data or, if agreed by the CAA, in accordance with the component maintenance data, only while such components are fitted to the aircraft. Nevertheless, such an A-rated maintenance organisation may temporarily remove a component for maintenance in order to improve access to that component, except when its removal generates the need for additional maintenance that the organisation is not approved to perform. Such removal of component for maintenance by A-rated maintenance organisation must be subject to an appropriate control procedure in the MOE. The limitation column must specify the scope of such maintenance in order to indicate the extent of the approval.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Category A class ratings are subdivided into “Base” or “Line” maintenance categories. Such an organisation may be approved for either “Base” or “Line” maintenance, or both. It should be noted that a “Line” facility located at a main base facility requires a “Line” maintenance approval.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: A “ category B class rating ” means that the maintenance organisation may carry out maintenance on uninstalled engines, APUs and engines, APU components or a combination of them, in accordance with the engine or APU maintenance data or both, or, if agreed by the CAA, in accordance with the component maintenance data, only while such components are fitted to the engine, the APU or both. Nevertheless, such a B-rated approved maintenance organisation may temporarily remove a component for maintenance in order to improve access to that component, except when its removal generates the need for additional maintenance that the organisation is not approved to perform. The limitation column must specify the scope of such maintenance, thereby indicating the extent of the approval. A maintenance organisation that is approved with a category B class rating may also carry out maintenance on an installed engine during aircraft base and line maintenance, provided that an appropriate control procedure in the MOE has been approved by the CAA. The scope of work in the MOE must reflect those activities if they are permitted by the CAA.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: A “ category C class rating ” means that the maintenance organisation may carry out maintenance on uninstalled components (excluding complete engines and APUs) that are intended to be fitted on the aircraft or the engine or APU. The limitation column must specify the scope of such maintenance, thereby indicating the extent of the approval. A maintenance organisation that is approved with a category C class rating may also carry out maintenance on an installed component (other than a complete engine or APU) during aircraft base and line maintenance, or at an engine or APU maintenance facility provided that an appropriate control procedure in the MOE has been approved by the CAA. The scope of work in the MOE must reflect those activities if they are permitted by the CAA.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: A “ category D class rating ” means a self-contained class rating that is not necessarily related to a specific aircraft, engine or other component. The D1 – Non-Destructive Testing (“ NDT ”) rating is only necessary for a maintenance organisation that carries out NDT as a particular task for another organisation. A maintenance organisation that is approved with a class rating in the A, B or C category may carry out NDT on products that it maintains without the need for a D1 class rating provided that the MOE contains appropriate NDT procedures.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The limitation column is intended to give the CAA the flexibility to customise an approval for any particular organisation. Ratings may only be mentioned on the approval if they are appropriately limited. The table in point (l) specifies the types of limitations that are possible. It is acceptable to stress in the limitation column the maintenance task rather than the type or manufacturer of the aircraft or engine, if that is more appropriate to the organisation (an example could be avionics systems installations and the related maintenance). If that is mentioned in the limitation column, it indicates that the maintenance organisation is approved to carry out maintenance up to and including that particular type or task.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: When reference is made to the series, type and group in the limitation column of class A and B, it must be understood as follows:

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: “ series ” means a specific type series such as the Airbus 300, 310, 319, the Boeing 737-300 series, RB211-524 series, Cessna 150, Cessna 172, Beech 55 series or the Continental O-200 series;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: “ type ” means a specific type or model such as the Airbus 310-240 type, the RB 211-524 B4 type, or the Cessna 172RG type. Any number of series or types may be quoted;

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: “ group ” means, for example, Cessna single piston engine aircraft or Lycoming non-supercharged piston engines, etc.

Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.

rows.text: Line maintenance certifying staff and base maintenance support staff shall demonstrate he/she received type training and passed examination at the category B1, B2 or B3 level, as applicable, referred to in Appendix III to Annex III (Part-66) for each aircraft type in the scope of work referred to in point (b). Those persons whose scope of work does not exceed those of a category A certifying staff may however receive task training in lieu of a complete type training.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Base maintenance certifying staff shall demonstrate he/she received type training and passed examination at the category C level referred to in Appendix III to Annex III (Part-66) for each aircraft type in the scope of work referred to in point (b), except that for the first aircraft type, training and examination shall be at the category B1, B2 or B3 level of Appendix III.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: 2. Protected rights U.K.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: The personnel having privileges before the entry into force of the relevant requirements of Annex III (Part-66) may continue to exercise them without the need to comply with points 1(c) to 1(f).

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: However after that date any certifying staff willing to extend the scope of their authorisation to include additional privileges shall comply with point 1.

rows.section_heading: Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
Immediate reaction to a safety problem U.K.
rows.text: Notwithstanding point 2(b) above, in the case of additional type training, compliance with points 1(c) and 1(d) is not required.
